cohort: 1134 low-risk women with singleton and at-term pregnancies were selected from a first-level hospital in Spain between 2009 and 2019.
finding: Women choosing water immersion for labor analgesia were significantly more likely to experience spontaneous vaginal birth and have an intact perineum, and their newborns showed better 5-minute Apgar scores, umbilical cord arterial pH, and lower NICU admission rates compared to those receiving epidural analgesia.
mod_finding: Spontaneous vaginal birth was almost 17 times more likely in the water immersion group, while the odds of having a cesarean birth were almost 40 times higher in the epidural group.
